page: Microsoft Azure E16d_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance belonging to the EDv4 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, offering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor features a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio, and includes 614 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark data places the E16d_v4 in the average performance tier across most metrics. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1287.0 and a multi-core score of 7924.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 831.21 GB/sec, which drops to 82.69 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 44.34 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance processes 13.96 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 5735.49 on PassMark database operations.

While the server demonstrates stable average performance for standard tasks, it exhibits limitations in intensive computational workloads. Specifically, LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model are weak, yielding 22.4 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 8.48 tokens/sec for text generation. Consequently, this instance is suited for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and general web serving rather than heavy AI model execution. The inclusion of local SSD storage and a high memory-to-core ratio provides a balanced resource density for enterprise database hosting.
